curated.instructions: omr/instructions/8419-1-1.pdf (the excavator, functions on pages 60-61; book 2, omr/instructions/8419-1-2.pdf, builds the alternate bulldozer)

functions.does: The upper body slews round on the turntable by hand, carrying the boom with it.
functions.source: book 1: page 60 (arrows round the turntable); steps 17-19 (turntable)

functions.does: The knob at the back on the right (a 20-tooth double bevel gear) raises and lowers the boom: it turns a worm, which turns a 24-tooth gear on a cross shaft at the back; cranks and a side link carry that to a cross shaft at the front, whose two arms push the boom up on two thin beams.
functions.source: book 1: page 61 (knobs and icons); steps 22 and 24 (boom raising, arrows), 23-28 (cranks and shafts), 29-30 (worm and 24-tooth gear), 32 and 36 (knobs, arrows)
functions.note: The drive from the cross shaft at the back (p170, p158) to the one at the front (p154, p142) is read from the model file: cranks p160 and p157 joined by a link at the left; check against a real model. The worm holds the boom wherever it's left.

functions.does: The knob at the back on the left (a 20-tooth double bevel gear) swings the stick in and out: through a 20- and a 16-tooth gear it turns a shaft that runs forward to a pair of 20-tooth bevel gears in the middle of the turntable, then up through a universal joint on the boom's pivot to a worm inside the boom, which turns an 8-tooth gear whose crank and links swing the stick and bucket at the boom's tip.
functions.source: book 1: page 60 (inset: bevel gear and universal joint at the centre), page 61 (knobs and icons); steps 6 (boom with worm, page 19), 19-21 (bevel gears, universal joint, boom on its pivot), 32 and 36 (knobs, arrows)
functions.note: Which knob does which is read from the gears in the model file: page 61 shows both knobs with an icon each but doesn't make clear which icon goes with which knob. The worm holds the stick wherever it's left.

functions.does: The two tracks run freely round their sprockets; nothing drives them.
The bucket is held at a fixed angle on the end of the stick by a grey link; it isn't worked separately.
functions.source: book 1: steps 42 and 46-48 (grey link and bucket); inferred: no separate control for it is built
